title: rollout-ux-canary-ab-backlog-grooming-notes
body:
Purpose:
This working note captures UX wireframe ideas and backlog grooming for the Rollouts console flows: canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. Goal is to converge on a single surface that lets engineers configure experiments and safety fallbacks with minimal ambiguity and strong observability hooks.

Status/context:
- Owner: Maya Chen (product)
- Current phase: internal wireframe + grooming. Seeking design feedback + engineering feasibility review before formal PRD.
- Related tickets: RINF-4212 (rollouts MVP), RINF-4301 (metrics widget), RINF-4389 (fallback-policy engine)

High-level UX principles:
1) Single-pane summary for each rollout: status, traffic split, active variants, SLOs, last health checks, and quick rollback.
2) Progressive disclosure: default ‘simple canary’ flow for quick deploys; advanced mode exposes A/B buckets, staged ramping schedules, and traffic routing rules.
3) Observability-first: show live TPS/latency/error-rate, token-cost delta, and a small sample of recent responses for each variant.
4) Safety: clear, visible fallback and automatic rollback controls; preview of fallback model/version and estimated failover latency.

Wireframe notes (desktop):
- Top bar: rollout name (editable), environment selector (hosted | dedicated | private), badge for state (draft | running | paused | failed).
- Left column (summary card): current traffic distribution donut, model variants listed (v1, v1-quant, v2-8bit), primary health indicator (green/yellow/red), quick actions (Pause, Promote, Rollback).
- Center (main flow editor): stepper with 3 tabs: Canary, A/B Test, Fallbacks. Default opens Canary.
    * Canary tab: small form: "percentage to canary" (slider 0-100), ramp schedule (immediate | linear over N minutes), evaluation window (X min), SLO guards (latency p50/p95, error-rate). Live preview of rollout timeline with annotations.
    * A/B Test tab: create variants (name, model version, per-variant weight), targeting rules (optional: route by customer ID hash, header-based routing), metric goals (primary metric: latency/cost/quality), analysis type (frequentist | bayesian).
    * Fallbacks tab: list of automatic fallback rules. Each rule: trigger (error-rate > X% for Y sec, latency p95 > Z ms, cost per-token > $T), action (failover to variant X, route to cheaper variant, degrade to cached responses, return canned response), notification channels (Slack, PagerDuty), cooldown period.
- Right column (observability stack): charts for last 30m: requests/sec (per-variant), token-cost/tokens, latency p50/p95, error-rate. Small table with sample request/responses (redacted), top failing routes, and active alerts.

Interaction details / microcopy suggestions:
- Slider label: "Canary share (%) — test new variant with X% of traffic"
- Ramp schedule tooltip: "Staged rollout reduces risk. Choose immediate for fast promotion."
- SLO guard flows: when SLO is breached, show a modal: "SLO guard triggered — automatic action: Pause rollout and trigger fallback to v1. Confirm or override?" with buttons: View evidence | Override & continue | Cancel rollout.
- On rollback: prompt with reason (required), estimated impact (delta in latency/cost), and a one-click rollback start button.

Backlog grooming items (candidate tickets + rough estimates):
- RINF-4502: Wireframe -> Figma conversion for main rollout console (8d)
- RINF-4503: Canary slider + ramp scheduling UI component (5d)
- RINF-4504: A/B variant editor + targeting rules (8d)
- RINF-4505: Fallback rule builder + triggers library (10d)
- RINF-4506: Observability widgets: per-variant charts + sample tracer integration (7d)
- RINF-4507: API contract for rollouts service (routes, POST /rollouts, PATCH /rollouts/:id/actions) (3d)
- RINF-4508: End-to-end e2e tests for rollback + fallback (5d)
- RINF-4509: Accessibility pass + keyboard-first interactions (3d)
Priority: implement Canary UI + basic Fallbacks first (RINF-4503, RINF-4505, RINF-4506, RINF-4507). A/B editor next.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP canary + fallback):
- Console: user can create a canary rollout from an existing model version, set a % share, choose ramp schedule, and hit "Start".
- Observability: live metrics update within 30s and show per-variant breakdown.
- Safety: user can configure at least one automatic fallback trigger (error-rate or latency) and select an action (failover or pause).
- Actionability: When fallback trigger fires, rollout pauses and fallback action executes automatically; the console records a time-stamped audit entry.
- API: POST /rollouts returns rollout id and current traffic distribution; PATCH /rollouts/:id/actions accepts pause/promote/rollback with reason.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we surface token-cost as a primary metric in the rollout summary or keep it in advanced mode? (Pros: cost-awareness; Cons: noise for quick dev flows)
- Default fallback action: Pause + notify vs immediate failover? Proposal: Pause + failover as two configurable toggles; default is Pause + notify for safety.
- A/B analysis: include automated significance detection? MVP: show raw numbers & confidence intervals; follow-up: add Bayesian stats.
- Targeting: level of granularity for hash-based targeting (customer id vs session id). Ops may prefer tenancy-level targeting for Dedicated customers.

UX edge cases to handle:
- Variant disappears (model undeployed) while rollout running: mark as orphaned and automatically reassign traffic to fallback variant, but flag for manual review.
- Overlapping rollouts for same route: disallow unless explicitly allowed by admin; show blocking dialog listing conflicting rollouts and owners.
- Private deployments (on-prem): hide hosted-only features (e.g., cross-region fallback) and surface network/latency caveats.

Operational notes for SRE / backend teams:
- Need a streaming channel for per-variant metrics with 15–30s granularity. Prefer pushing via existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> metrics service) and a small rollouts metrics adapter that exposes per-rollout labels.
- Rollout control plane should authoritatively store: rollout config, active traffic allocation, evaluation windows, and history of actions (audit).
- Fallback execution must be idempotent and have retries with exponential backoff; must emit events to eventstore for console to display.

Next steps / owners:
- Maya: finalize Figma wireframes (target 2026-03-17) -> RINF-4502
- Arjun: feasibility check for metrics adapter and API schema (complete by 2026-03-12)
- Lena: prototype A/B editor interactions (prototype due 2026-03-24)
- Diego: draft fallback triggers spec with SRE (RINF-4389 follow-up)

Notes to self / rough ideas to capture later:
- Quick 'promote' UX: after canary meets SLOs for N windows, offer a one-click 'Promote to 100%' with a short cooldown.
- Include a cost-savings estimator when suggesting a fallback to a quantized variant.
- Consider a 'run locally' button to simulate rollout on a small synthetic traffic sample for privacy-sensitive environments.

Links and references:
- Confluence: rollout-flows-v0 (design history)
- Slack thread: #prod-console — discussion around "default-fallback" (p/abc123)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/834 (metrics-panel spike)

Unresolved UX nit: copy for the "Pause vs Failover" modal. Current candidate: "Safety triggers observed — pause rollout and alert team, or immediately switch traffic to the fallback variant. Pausing is reversible; failing over may expose older model behavior."

End of notes.
